**Yes.** As an opening, the passage rightly compresses a great deal of story time: ten years of exile, repeated petitions to the Council, the shift in Casanova's tone from defiance to remorse, the fading of his sins, and his countless retellings of the escape from the Leads. All of this fits into long, flowing periodic sentences that work as efficient exposition. The bird image of circling ever lower gives this summarized span emotional weight without stalling the narrative.

The second paragraph then narrows to the present situation: two months in Mantua, a modest inn, and the waiting filled with writing the polemic against Voltaire. This slows the narrative toward the scene-level time where the story proper will begin. Moving from broad summary of the past to a tighter focus on the present feels deliberate and well proportioned, so the pacing suits the passage's role of setting up the story.
